jobs.title: Principal Electrical Engineer (Portal)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role:

Northwood is looking for a Principal Electrical Engineer to help drive the development of our digital compute and power electronics. These complex digital systems ensure that our antennas can meet high-rate processing needs no matter where they are deployed around the world. Our hardware team prioritizes excellent engineering, building end products that are known for their reliability, scalability, and cost.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Drive electrical design for high-speed digital communication systems, implementing RF and mixed-signal designs in complex, multilayer PCBs

  • Work with 100G high speed networking, complex digital power trees, and drive system trades for architecture decisions

  • Perform schematic capture, layout, and bring-up on a variety of different digital systems including FPGAs, microcontrollers, and their associated peripherals

  • Collaborate across hardware and software teams with RF engineers, antenna engineers, FPGA engineers, and firmware engineers to optimize system performance and overall design

  • Test prototypes and assess performance in the lab and in the field

  • Work with production teams to make testable and manufacturable products that we can integrate in-house

 

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field

  • 8+ years of professional experience in electrical design

  • Experience with end-to-end board design, from architecture and component selection through schematic capture, PCB layout, bring-up, debug, and production

  • Experience with mixed-signal electronics design and complex multilayer PCBs, including stack-up definition and material selection

  • Experience with troubleshooting EMI/EMC, either conducted or radiated

     

Preferred Qualifications:

  • High-speed digital design experience with interfaces such as multi-gigabit SerDes, DDR, JESD204B/C, and 10/100G Ethernet, including signal and power integrity analysis

  • Experience with FPGA-or processor-based systems and high-speed data converters

  • Deep understanding of signal integrity, power integrity, EMI/EMC mitigation, PCB stack-up definition, and high-performance board layout practices

  • Hands-on experience debugging complex hardware systems using advanced lab instrumentation and driving root-cause analysis across board and system levels

  • Ability to lead cross-functional technical efforts, mentor junior engineers, and make sound engineering tradeoffs in fast-paced development environments

jobs.title: RF Systems Engineer (Portal)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role:
As an RF Systems Engineer you will define and evaluate phased-array RF architectures for Northwood’s satellite ground-station network. You will translate mission and link requirements into antenna, aperture, beamforming, RF front-end, calibration, and tracking requirements, and evaluate how those choices affect end-to-end communications performance.


This role sits at the intersection of phased arrays, RF systems, SATCOM links, and physical-layer communications. You will work closely with antenna, RF, DSP/communications, digital, mechanical, manufacturing, software, and operations teams to ensure that the complete ground-station system achieves its required link performance.


The ideal candidate has deep experience in phased-array or antenna systems and can reason beyond the aperture—connecting gain, scan loss, polarization, sidelobes, noise, linearity, phase noise, calibration, and propagation to EVM, acquisition, BER, throughput, and link availability.


Responsibilities:

  • Define phased-array antenna and RF-system architectures for satellite communication ground stations.

  • Translate mission, coverage, link-availability, waveform, throughput, and regulatory requirements into aperture, RF front-end, beamforming, calibration, pointing, and tracking specifications.

  • Develop and maintain end-to-end SATCOM link budgets incorporating measured aperture and RF-chain performance.

  • Analyze analog, hybrid, and digital beamforming approaches in collaboration with RF and digital implementation teams.

  • Determine how antenna and RF impairments affect communications performance, including EVM, carrier acquisition, BER/BLER, throughput, spectral compliance, and link availability.

  • Analyze RF lineups and performance budgets for gain, noise figure, dynamic range, linearity, compression, intermodulation, phase noise, frequency stability, filtering, and isolation.

  • Build Python, MATLAB, or similar models combining array behavior, measured RF performance, propagation, and modem-level metrics.

  • Lead cross-functional investigations of degraded G/T, EIRP, link margin, EVM, acquisition, tracking, BER, throughput, or spectral performance.

  • Support regulatory submissions, spectrum coordination, partner interface reviews, system acceptance, and operational deployment.

     

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Electrical Engineering, Communications Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related discipline.

  • 2+ years of experience with phased arrays, antenna systems, RF communication systems, or SATCOM terminals.

  • Experience with communication-link analysis, including EIRP, G/T, C/N0​, Eb​/N0​, link margin, atmospheric loss, and interference.

  • Understanding of digital communications sufficient to relate RF performance to modulation-dependent EVM, acquisition, BER, throughput, and spectral performance.

  • Experience defining or evaluating RF lineups, including noise figure, gain, linearity, dynamic range, phase noise, filtering, and isolation.

  • Hands-on experience with RF measurements and integrated system debugging using equipment such as vector network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, noise sources, and vector signal analyzers.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with SATCOM waveforms and standards such as DVB-S2/S2X, CCSDS, or equivalent modem architectures.

  • Experience analyzing modulation-dependent EVM, BER/BLER, adjacent-channel leakage, spectral regrowth, amplifier backoff, and link degradation.

  • Experience with SDR-integrated RF systems or collaboration with FPGA, DSP, modem, and embedded-software teams.

  • Experience with HFSS, CST, or comparable full-wave electromagnetic tools.

  • Familiarity with radar, sensing, 5G NR, 802.11ad/ay, MIMO, multi-beam systems, or electronic-warfare systems where the experience transfers to array and RF-system architecture.

 

Additional Requirements:

  • Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed

 

Compensation:

RF/Antenna Engineer/Level 1: $104,000 - $130,000 per year

RF/Antenna Engineer/Level 2: $124,000 - $155,000 per year

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role

Northwood Space is looking for an experienced, hands-on specialist to deploy and maintain our ground sites around the world. You'll independently install, test, and repair ground station hardware, and represent Northwood professionally as our on-site subject matter expert while working away from the factory.

Responsibilities

  • Deploy new sites independently, leading local contractor crews through mechanical, electrical, and network equipment installation.

  • Install and integrate site hardware, including antenna assemblies, equipment racks, cabling, motors, and power distribution equipment.

  • Commission new installations: inspect the build, power up systems, run functional tests, verify operation, and find and fix issues before handoff.

  • Maintain deployed sites and resolve field issues on your own, using test equipment, schematics, and technical documentation to isolate faults down to the component level.

  • Make sound decisions in the field and escalate safety, design, or scope concerns when needed.

  • Document work performed, test results, open issues, and field findings, and turn them into procedures that help engineering, production, and future field crews.

  • Own the deployment area and field kits, so every deployment and maintenance trip has the right tools, spares, and equipment.

  • Help build work-order and issue tracking for field operations.

  • Support integration, testing, and improvements at the Torrance facility between deployments.

Required Qualifications

  • At least five years of hands-on experience installing, integrating, testing, or servicing complex electromechanical systems.

  • A track record of completing technical work and resolving problems with little or no on-site supervision.

  • Experience directing contractors or technicians who are less familiar with the equipment.

  • Comfort with hand and power tools, crimping and termination, and electrical test equipment.

  • Ability to work from mechanical drawings, electrical schematics, and procedures.

  • Willingness and ability to travel approximately 50–75% of the time, including to remote sites and internationally.

  • Strong safety, communication, and organization practices.

  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work outdoors in varied weather conditions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Aerospace or satellite ground systems experience, particularly with deployed hardware.

  • Rack-mounted hardware and network equipment, including servers, switches, and fiber and copper cabling.

  • Low-voltage AC/DC power systems, wire harnesses, motors and drives, and control systems.

  • Antennas, RF-adjacent equipment, or communications systems.

  • Both new-site commissioning and ongoing maintenance or repair of equipment already in service.

  • Building or using work-order systems, maintenance logs, or field-operations dashboards.

  • Operating lifts, forklifts, or other heavy equipment.

Level 3: $42.00 - $51.00/hour

jobs.title: Software Engineer- Early Career (Platform)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role

Northwood engineers and operators run hardware and software across a global network of antenna ground stations and the cloud services behind them. No one sells a platform for running a network like this at scale, so Northwood builds its own.

Platform Engineering builds the software that takes Northwood products from first prototype to full operation. That covers how code is built, tested, and released, how every site and service is monitored, and how hardware in remote locations is brought online, updated, and kept healthy. Every one of these problems has to work across every site, service, and customer at once.

Few organizations get to build this kind of software in house. What this team builds will shape how a global network of antennas is operated for the missions that depend on it. Every new antenna, site, and customer Northwood adds runs on this platform, and it sets how fast the network can grow.

As an early-career Software Engineer on the Platform team, you'll ship to real production systems from your first weeks, with close mentorship, and take on more ownership as you show you're ready. You don't need to know every part of the stack today. You need to learn fast, reason clearly through problems you haven't seen before, and care a lot about what you build.

Key areas of focus

You'll work across these areas over time. No one is expected to own everything listed.

  • Delivery and release

    • Build the CI and release pipelines that take code from commit to production, in the cloud and at ground stations around the world.

    • Make shipping safe and continuous, with staged rollouts and fast rollback, so no one has to test in production.

  • Simulation and test

    • Build simulated ground stations and lab test benches running real hardware, so every release is tested against realistic conditions before it reaches a live site.

    • Build tools that replay real recorded data through the system to catch problems early.

  • Ground station operations

    • Automate how new sites are brought online, configured, and updated, in remote locations with few or no people on site.

    • Write software that runs on the servers that sit next to the antennas, and keep a global fleet of them healthy.

  • Observability

    • Build the monitoring, logging, and alerting that show the health of every service and site.

    • Turn raw telemetry into signals engineers and operators can act on before a problem reaches a customer.

  • Internal platform and tools

    • Build the backend services and web interfaces engineers and operators use every day to create, ship, and run software.

    • Talk directly with the people who use what you build, and turn their feedback into improvements.

  • Infrastructure and security

    • Define the cloud and site infrastructure the platform runs on as code.

    • Build identity, secrets management, and least-privilege access into the platform, so every service gets them by default.

Basic Qualifications

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role:

As our first Cost Accountant, you will build and own the cost accounting function as we scale our space infrastructure products from development into production. You will establish the processes, methodologies, and controls that give the company accurate visibility into inventory, COGS, and the true cost of building our hardware while owning the day-to-day cost accounting activities required to support the business today. Working closely with Finance, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Engineering, and Program teams, you will create a scalable cost accounting foundation that supports a rapidly growing organization and increasingly complex manufacturing operations.

Responsibilities:

  • Build and own the company’s cost accounting function, establishing scalable processes, methodologies, controls, documentation, and reporting for inventory, standard costs, WIP, COGS, and manufacturing variances as production scales.

  • Own cost accounting activities across month-end and quarter-end close, including journal entries, inventory and cost account reconciliations, accruals, variance analysis, and supporting schedules, ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting.

  • Develop and maintain standard costing methodologies across purchased and manufactured hardware; analyze purchase price, material, labor, overhead, absorption, scrap, and other variances to identify root causes and improve cost accuracy.

  • Own inventory accounting and valuation across raw materials, WIP, and finished goods, partnering with Supply Chain and Manufacturing to reconcile operational activity to the ERP and resolve inventory, work order, and transaction discrepancies.

  • Partner closely with Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Program teams to understand BOMs, production flows, procurement costs, engineering changes, and operational drivers, translating them into accurate product costs and actionable financial insights.

  • Serve as the Finance owner for cost accounting systems and continuous improvement, helping define ERP requirements, automate manual processes, strengthen financial controls, and build the reporting infrastructure needed to support significant company and production growth.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field with 4+ years of experience in cost accounting, inventory accounting, or manufacturing accounting.

  • Strong understanding of manufacturing cost accounting, including standard costing, inventory valuation, WIP, COGS, PPV, absorption, manufacturing variances, and inventory flows within an ERP environment.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently own cost accounting close activities, journal entries, reconciliations, and complex analyses while identifying and resolving discrepancies across financial and operational data.

  • Highly analytical and comfortable operating autonomously in a fast-paced environment, with strong Excel skills and demonstrated ability to build processes, solve ambiguous problems, and partner effectively across Finance and Operations.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in aerospace, defense, hardware, automotive, electronics, or another complex manufacturing environment, particularly within a startup or rapidly scaling organization.

  • Experience building or significantly improving cost accounting processes, controls, standard costing methodologies, and reporting as manufacturing operations scale.

  • Experience partnering directly with Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Engineering, and other operational teams and translating manufacturing activity into financial insights and recommendations.

  • Experience implementing, configuring, or improving cost accounting and inventory workflows within an ERP system, including supporting system requirements, testing, data validation, and process automation.

Role

Northwood Space is looking for a Tax Accountant to help build the tax function. You will own day-to-day tax activities, coordinate with external advisors, and establish scalable processes that support our expanding operations. Working closely with Finance, Accounting, Legal, and operational teams, you will bring structure to complex tax matters and help the company make informed business decisions as we continue to grow and scale.

Responsibilities

  • Own the tax compliance calendar and coordinate federal, state and local filings with external advisors, ensuring accurate supporting schedules, timely submissions, and appropriate documentation.

  • Manage sales and use tax compliance, including registrations, nexus assessments, exemption certificates, and evaluating the tax treatment of ground station services and equipment purchases.

  • Support income tax provisions, tax account reconciliations, estimated payments, and financial reporting by preparing workpapers and coordinating technical reviews with external tax specialists.

  • Partner with Finance, Legal, and business teams to assess tax considerations for new ground station locations, customer contracts, capital investments, and expansion into new jurisdictions.

  • Build scalable tax processes, internal controls, and documentation; improve ERP tax configurations and data quality; and serve as the primary internal contact for tax notices, audits, and advisor requests.

  • Identify and evaluate potential tax credits, incentives, and opportunities in partnership with external advisors, including those related to research and development, manufacturing, and infrastructure investment.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 3+ years of tax experience in public accounting, corporate tax, or a combination, with hands-on experience preparing or reviewing tax filings and supporting schedules.

  • Working knowledge of U.S. federal and state business taxation, including income tax and sales and use tax, with the ability to research unfamiliar issues and recognize when specialist guidance is needed.

  • Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills, with proficiency in Excel and accounting systems and the ability to independently manage deadlines and build processes in an evolving environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • CPA designation, progress toward CPA licensure, or a graduate degree in Taxation or Accounting.

  • Experience at a startup or growing company, particularly in aerospace, telecommunications, infrastructure, manufacturing, or another business with significant physical assets.

  • Exposure to international tax compliance, VAT/GST, transfer pricing, or tax considerations associated with operating across multiple jurisdictions.

We're looking for a Software Engineer on the Platform team to design and build this software end to end, from backend services and automation to the interfaces people use every day. The role is broad, across backend, frontend, CI/CD, infrastructure, and security, and you'll own major parts of the platform.

We look for people who fix problems they find even when they aren't theirs, move quickly from question to working result, hold their own work to a high bar, take hard feedback well, and want more responsibility than they have today.

  • Developer environments: Build fast local development, a preview environment for each change, and safe access to cloud and site systems.

  • Ownership: Own what you ship in production: monitoring, on-call for your systems, and fixing root causes.

  • Hands-on experience with several of the following, or their equivalents:

    • Containers and container orchestration (such as Docker and Kubernetes)

    • A cloud platform (such as AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure)

    • Infrastructure as code (such as Terraform or CloudFormation)

    • Relational databases (such as PostgreSQL or MySQL)

    • Linux and the command line

  • Has owned a service, tool, or platform from design through production, with other engineers or users relying on it, including working through at least one hard problem along the way (such as a difficult production bug, a design under real constraints, or a significant migration).

  • Has written technical documents other engineers used, such as design docs, RFCs, or runbooks.

Preferred Qualifications

Strong candidates bring depth in a few of these. No one has all of them.

  • Depth in a systems or backend language (such as Rust, Go, or Python), or equivalent.

  • Built web applications end to end, from the API to the interface, with a modern frontend framework (such as React, Vue, or Angular).

  • Built developer platforms, internal tools, or self-service infrastructure that other engineers relied on.

  • Cut friction for other engineers and measured whether it worked, such as faster onboarding, fewer support requests, or higher adoption.

  • Designed CI/CD pipelines or release systems that ship to many environments or locations, including GitOps-style deployment (such as Argo CD or Flux).

  • Deployed and operated services on Kubernetes or an equivalent, with packaging tools (such as Helm).

  • Built test infrastructure, such as simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, test data replay, or shared test harnesses (such as pytest-based frameworks).

  • Ran production systems with metrics, logs, and dashboards (such as Prometheus, Grafana, or Datadog), including on-call and incident response.

That covers how code is built, tested, and released, how every site and service is monitored, and how hardware in remote locations is brought online, updated, and kept healthy. The problems span CI and release, observability, hardware operations, developer tooling, and security, and every one of them has to work across every site, service, and customer at once.

Few organizations get to build this kind of software in house. What this team builds will shape how a global network of antennas is operated for the missions that depend on it. Every new antenna, site, and customer Northwood adds runs on this platform, and it sets how fast the network can grow. The work includes simulated ground stations and lab test benches running real hardware, where each release is tested against realistic conditions before it reaches a live site.

We're looking for a Software Engineer on the Platform team to design and build this software end to end, from backend services and automation to the interfaces people use every day. The role is broad, across backend, frontend, CI/CD, infrastructure, and security, and you'll own major parts of the platform.

We look for people who fix problems they find even when they aren't theirs, move quickly from question to working result, hold their own work to a high bar, take hard feedback well, and want more responsibility than they have today.




RESPONSIBILITIES

You'll work across these areas and own more of them over time.

 - Delivery: Build the CI and release systems that take code from commit to production in the cloud and at sites around the world, safely and repeatably.

 - Testing and simulation: Build simulated ground stations, lab test benches with real hardware, and test data replay, and wire them into the release path so releases are tested before they go live.

 - Observability: Build the monitoring, logging, and alerting that let engineers and operators see the health of every service and site, and act on it.

 - Hardware operations: Automate how new sites are brought online, configured, updated, and kept healthy, in locations with few or no people on site.

 - Self-service tools: Build the tools and web interfaces engineers and operators use to create, ship, and run software without waiting on another team.

 - Security by default: Build identity, secrets management, least-privilege access, and audit into the platform, so every service gets them without extra work.

 - Infrastructure: Define the cloud and site infrastructure the platform runs on as code, so it is reviewed, versioned, and repeatable.

 - Developer environments: Build fast local development, a preview environment for each change, and safe access to cloud and site systems.

 - Ownership: Own what you ship in production: monitoring, on-call for your systems, and fixing root causes.

 - Working with users: Gather requirements directly from the engineers and operators who use the platform, write clear design docs, ship in small steps, and take part in design and code reviews.




BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, writing production code in at least one general-purpose language (such as Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, or Java).

 - Has built backend services or APIs (such as REST or gRPC) that other systems or people depend on.

 - Hands-on experience with several of the following, or their equivalents:
   
   - CI/CD pipelines (such as GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Jenkins)
   
   - Containers and container orchestration (such as Docker and Kubernetes)
   
   - A cloud platform (such as AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure)
   
   - Infrastructure as code (such as Terraform or CloudFormation)
   
   - Relational databases (such as PostgreSQL or MySQL)
   
   - Linux and the command line

 - Has owned a service, tool, or platform from design through production, with other engineers or users relying on it, including working through at least one hard problem along the way (such as a difficult production bug, a design under real constraints, or a significant migration).

 - Has written technical documents other engineers used, such as design docs, RFCs, or runbooks.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Strong candidates bring depth in a few of these. No one has all of them.

 - Depth in a systems or backend language (such as Rust, Go, or Python), or equivalent.

 - Built web applications end to end, from the API to the interface, with a modern frontend framework (such as React, Vue, or Angular).

 - Built developer platforms, internal tools, or self-service infrastructure that other engineers relied on.

 - Cut friction for other engineers and measured whether it worked, such as faster onboarding, fewer support requests, or higher adoption.

 - Designed CI/CD pipelines or release systems that ship to many environments or locations, including GitOps-style deployment (such as Argo CD or Flux).

 - Deployed and operated services on Kubernetes or an equivalent, with packaging tools (such as Helm).

 - Built test infrastructure, such as simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, test data replay, or shared test harnesses (such as pytest-based frameworks).

 - Ran production systems with metrics, logs, and dashboards (such as Prometheus, Grafana, or Datadog), including on-call and incident response.

 - Worked with identity and access (such as Okta or Auth0), secrets management (such as HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager), or regulated environments (such as AWS GovCloud).

 - Managed fleets of on-premises or edge servers, including declarative configuration (such as Nix, Ansible, or Puppet).

 - Exposure to hardware, embedded, RF, or space systems.



Additional Information:

jobs.title: Cost Accounting Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role:

As our first Cost Accounting Manager, you will build and lead the cost accounting function as we scale our space infrastructure products from development into production. You will establish the strategy, policies, processes, and controls that provide accurate visibility into inventory, COGS, and the true cost of building our hardware while maintaining hands-on ownership of core accounting activities. Working closely with Finance, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Engineering, and Program teams, you will guide decisions on product costs, production efficiency, and inventory management while developing the systems and team capabilities needed to support increasingly complex manufacturing operations.

Responsibilities:

  • Build and lead the company’s cost accounting function, defining policies, methodologies, controls, reporting, and team development priorities for inventory, standard costs, WIP, COGS, and manufacturing variances as production scales.

  • Lead cost accounting activities across month-end and quarter-end close, preparing and reviewing journal entries, reconciliations, accruals, variance analyses, and supporting schedules to ensure accurate, timely financial reporting in accordance with US GAAP.

  • Establish and oversee standard costing methodologies for purchased and manufactured hardware, including labor and overhead rates; investigate material variances and guide cross-functional actions to improve cost accuracy, production efficiency, and margins.

  • Own inventory accounting policies and valuation across raw materials, WIP, and finished goods, including reserves, excess and obsolete inventory, and physical inventory controls; partner with operational teams to resolve discrepancies and maintain audit readiness.

  • Serve as a financial partner to Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Program leadership, translating production activity, BOM changes, procurement trends, and capacity assumptions into product cost insights, cost reduction opportunities, and planning recommendations.

  • Lead cost accounting systems and process improvements, setting ERP requirements, strengthening controls, automating workflows, and developing scalable reporting while building and mentoring the cost accounting team as business needs grow.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field with 7+ years of progressive experience in cost accounting, inventory accounting, or manufacturing accounting, including experience leading accounting processes, projects, or teams.

  • Strong knowledge of US GAAP and manufacturing cost accounting, including standard costing, inventory valuation and reserves, WIP, COGS, purchase price variances, overhead allocation, absorption, and manufacturing inventory flows within an ERP environment.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead cost accounting close and reporting, establish accounting policies and controls, review complex analyses, and resolve discrepancies across financial and operational data.

  • Strong analytical, communication, and leadership skills, with advanced Excel proficiency and the ability to build processes, prioritize competing needs, and influence cross-functional decisions in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in aerospace, defense, hardware, automotive, electronics, or another complex manufacturing environment, particularly within a startup or rapidly scaling organization.

  • Experience building or scaling a cost accounting function, including establishing standard costing methodologies, inventory controls, management reporting, and team responsibilities.

  • Experience partnering with operational leadership to drive measurable improvements in product costs, manufacturing efficiency, inventory management, and financial performance.

  • Experience leading ERP implementations or improvements across cost accounting and inventory workflows, including requirements definition, testing, data validation, process automation, and user adoption.

Additional Information:

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

jobs.title: Development Test Engineer (Portal)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role:

Northwood is looking for an engineer to build the development systems that ensure our hardware performs reliably from early prototypes through operations. You’ll own development test including hardware-in-the-loop testbeds, development RF testbeds or ranges/chambers, and customer integration milestones for modem test. This is a highly hands-on role that sits at the intersection of electronics, software, and systems integration — ideal for someone who enjoys turning ambiguous problems into robust, repeatable test capabilities that help develop world-class systems.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead integrated test development from concept through operations, including test strategy, requirements, and execution plans

  • Own the path to certification for EMI/EMC and other applicable standards (e.g., MIL-STD-461, FCC/CE), including pre-compliance testing, design-for-compliance input to the hardware team, test lab coordination, and certification documentation

  • Design hardware, wiring, and electrical systems to support electrical and RF testing for development and production (fixtures, harnesses, interfaces, rack integration)

  • Create device and subsystem simulators for hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) and integrate testbeds into our CI/CD pipeline

  • Own test maintainability and reliability across the lifecycle, defining calibration, upkeep, debugging, and continuous improvement of test assets

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, or related field

  • Hands-on experience in Linux-based environment, and familiarity with basic computer networking

  • Hands-on experience with electrical test equipment such as power supplies, DC loads, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and spectrum analyzers

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience root-causing issues in integrated electronics (mixed-signal, digital, RF-adjacent systems)

  • Hands-on EMC test and troubleshooting experience, such as near-field probes, radiated emissions testing

  • Familiarity with MIL-STD-461 EMI/EMC requirements and MIL-STD-810 environmental test methods, including vibration, shock, and thermal testing

  • Experience building RF test setups for communications systems, including over-the-air and conducted testing, channel emulation, and modem or link-level performance characterization

  • Experience building hardware-in-the-loop testbeds and device simulators, and running them in automated CI environments

  • Experience designing test racks and harnessing

Compensation:

Test Engineer/Level 2: $100,000-$119,000 per year

Test Engineer/Level 3: $118,000-$148,000 per year

Test Engineer/Level 4: $136,000-$170,000 per year

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role:

As a Lifecycle Electrical Engineer, you will be responsible for operating and improving the world’s most capable ground segment network. You will own the designs of deployed modules and circuitry spanning RF, power, and high-speed digital electronics. You will drive investigations into fielded systems and develop component and subsystem updates to fielded designs.

Responsibilities:

  • Own electronics systems deployed in Prism systems from cradle to grave, spanning RF, power, and high-speed digital electronics

  • Observe performance and degradation of electronics deployed on Prism systems

  • Drive root cause investigations and corrective actions on in factory and deployed ground station

  • Provide design and analysis inputs to drive reliable design, test, and qualification campaigns

  • Drive design improvements to modules, from design to schematic capture to layout, manufacture, and deployment

  • Test prototypes and assess performance in the lab and in the field

  • Work with production teams to make testable and manufacturable products that we can integrate in-house

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics or a related field

  • 2-4+ years of professional experience in electrical design

  • Experience with end-to-end board design, from architecture and component selection through schematic capture, PCB layout, bring-up, debug, and production

  • Hands-on experience debugging complex hardware systems using advanced lab instrumentation and driving root-cause analysis across board and system levels

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience driving root cause and corrective action campaigns with thorough and systemic processes: fish bone, 5 Whys, etc.

  • Hands-on project team experience (Formula SAE, rocketry, CubeSat, etc.)

  • Deep understanding of signal integrity, power integrity, EMI/EMC mitigation, PCB stack-up definition, and high-performance board layout practices

  • RF design or test experience with LNAs, power amplifiers, filters, or up/down converters (gain, noise figure, compression, spurious)

  • High-speed digital design experience with FPGAs, SerDes, data converters, or 10/100G Ethernet, including signal and power integrity analysis

  • Power electronics design experience, such as DC-DC converters, sequencing, and protection circuits

  • Experience with troubleshooting EMI/EMC, either conducted or radiated

  • Experience with mixed-signal electronics design and complex multilayer PCBs, including stack-up definition and material selection

Compensation:

Electrical Engineer/Level 2: $125,000-$145,000 per year

jobs.title: Electronics Specialist (Prism)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role:

Northwood is seeking an Electronics Specialist to build and operate the hands-on test infrastructure that enables rapid hardware iteration from prototype through integration and qualification. In this role, you’ll assemble and troubleshoot test racks and setups, perform benchtop and integrated testing, and support environmental and system-level test campaigns with high-quality documentation and traceability. You’ll work closely with test engineers and hardware teams to debug anomalies, execute rework, fabricate harnessing and RF assemblies, and maintain a well-run lab environment. This is a highly hands-on role for someone who thrives in fast-paced development environments and enjoys turning scrappy prototypes into repeatable test setups that accelerate learning and reliability.

Responsibilities:

  • Build, wire, and troubleshoot test racks, fixtures, and mechanical/electrical test setups

  • Perform benchtop and integrated testing independently or with engineers, following procedures and requirements

  • Execute SMT + through-hole solder rework and fabricate harnesses/coax assemblies

  • Support integration and environmental test (repeatable configs, calibration/traceability, documentation)

  • Summarize and share test data and preliminary results, and support anomaly investigations to resolution

  • Maintain lab readiness (calibrated instrumentation, equipment health, tooling, consumables, organization)

  • Drive 5S and process improvements to improve throughput and reliability

  • Help develop safe work practices for high voltage / high power RF systems

  • Partner with test engineers to improve rack maintainability, documentation, and throughput

Basic Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate

  • 6+ years of experience as an electronics technician, test technician, or specialist supporting complex hardware

Role:
Northwood is looking for a Senior Electrical Engineer to own the non-RF electronics design for Prism, our 2.4-meter parabolic antenna for high-throughput satellite links. You will design the digital compute, power, embedded, and mixed-signal hardware that sits alongside Prism's RF chain- from block diagram and component selection through schematic, layout, bring-up, and production release.

Responsibilities

  • Own the electrical design of Prism's non-RF electronics: high-speed digital, power electronics, embedded control, and mixed-signal circuits

  • Architect and design high-density boards built around FPGAs, microcontrollers, high-speed data converters, and their peripherals, including DDR memory, multi-gigabit SerDes, and 10/100G Ethernet

  • Define clocking architectures: reference selection, clock distribution, jitter budgets, and synchronization across boards and subsystems

  • Design power trees end to end, from input power and conversion stages to point-of-load regulators, sequencing, monitoring, and protection

  • Design mixed-signal interfaces between digital and analog/RF domains, including ADC/DAC front ends, control loops, and sensor and telemetry circuits

  • Drive schematic capture, define PCB stack-ups, and lead layout of complex multilayer boards with a focus on signal integrity, power integrity, and EMI/EMC

  • Lead board bring-up and design verification, characterizing performance in the lab and iterating designs for performance, cost, and manufacturability

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering or a related engineering discipline

  • 5+ years of professional experience designing electronics hardware, with ownership of boards from schematic through bring-up

  • Hands-on design experience with high-speed digital systems built around FPGAs and/or microcontrollers

  • Experience designing board-level clocking and power distribution for complex digital systems

  • Proficiency in schematic capture, PCB stack-up definition, and layout of complex multilayer boards

  • Working knowledge of signal integrity, power integrity, and EMI/EMC design practices

Preferred Qualifications

  • Design experience with dense, high-pin-count FPGAs (e.g., AMD/Xilinx UltraScale+ or RFSoC) and the DDR, SerDes, and JESD204B/C interfaces around them

  • Low-jitter clock design: PLLs, jitter cleaners, clock fan-out, and clocking for high-speed data converters

  • Power electronics design: DC-DC converters, multiphase and point-of-load regulators, sequencing, hot-swap, and protection circuits

  • Embedded hardware design for microcontroller-based control and monitoring, with common interfaces such as I2C, SPI, UART, CAN, and Ethernet

  • Mixed-signal design, including precision analog, data converter front ends, and sensor interfaces

  • Lab skills with oscilloscopes, spectrum and network analyzers, and electronic loads, plus soldering and hot air rework

  • Python (or similar) for test automation and data analysis

Electrical Engineer/Level 3: $122,400-$153,000 per year

Electrical Engineer/Level 4: $144,000-$180,000 per year

Role:

The Incoming Quality Technician manages daily operations of the Incoming Inspection Room, including inspection tools, fixtures, calibration, and ESD controls. The technician verifies incoming PCBs, PCBAs, machined and welded mechanical parts, and other supplier materials against drawings and approved inspection requirements. The role works with Supplier Quality (SQE) and Engineering to resolve inspection issues and prevent nonconforming material from entering production. The technician also supports engineering samples, product verification, and drawing and DFM improvements through accurate measurement data.

Responsibilities:

  • Inspect incoming PCB/PCBA and mechanical parts against drawings, specifications, approved inspection plans, and applicable IPC-A-600 and IPC-A-610 criteria, using critical-characteristic checks, 100% inspection, or AQL sampling as specified.

  • Apply Northwood Space’s T1 (Production) and T2 (Engineering/R&D) part pedigree requirements; verify supplier CoCs, inspection reports, traceability records, and applicable FAI/PPAP documentation and approval status.

  • Manage the Incoming Inspection Room, including measurement tools, equipment, custom fixtures, calibration schedules, records, and calibration providers; maintain ESD controls and handling practices in accordance with ANSI/ESD S20.20.

  • Record inspection results and material traceability in the manufacturing system; identify and transfer nonconforming material to the MRB cage and coordinate disposition with the Supplier Quality Engineer (SQE) and Responsible Engineer (RE).

  • Provide dimensional measurement, inspection, and product verification support for engineering samples, prototypes, and first articles; conduct Gage Repeatability and Reproducibility (Gage R&R) studies to verify measurement system capability.

  • Share inspection data and feedback with Engineering and suppliers to support drawing corrections, design for manufacturability (DFM) improvements, and supplier quality investigations.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of hands-on incoming or quality inspection experience with PCB/PCBA and/or mechanical parts, including working knowledge of IPC-A-600 / IPC-A-610 acceptance criteria and ESD controls and handling practices.

  • Proficiency in interpreting PCB/PCBA and complex mechanical engineering drawings, including GD&T, datum references, dimensional tolerances, and critical characteristics; ability to follow risk-based inspection plans, including 100% inspection and AQL sampling.

  • Hands-on proficiency with precision measurement and inspection equipment, including handheld tools, VMMs, optical inspection systems, and custom fixtures, plus experience managing calibration schedules, status tracking, and records.

  • Experience identifying and documenting nonconforming materials, communicating quality issues to Supplier Quality (SQE) and Engineering, and using Manufacturo or similar ERP/MES systems to record inspection results, maintain material traceability, and manage NCR/MRB processes.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in aerospace, high-reliability electronics, or electromechanical manufacturing; familiarity with AS9100.

  • Experience managing calibration programs, using ISO/IEC 17025-accredited calibration providers, and supporting Gage R&R or other measurement system studies.

  • Familiarity with APQP, PPAP, AS9102 FAI, and different quality and inspection requirements based on part pedigree as (Production) and (Engineering/R&D).

  • Experience with PCB/ PCBA inspection (e.g., bow/twist, holes, plating, surface finish) and mechanical machining or weld inspection.

  • IPC-A-600 or IPC-A-610 certification.

  • Experience with CMM

Additional Information:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role:

Northwood is hiring a Regulatory Engineer to help license our global ground station network. Working directly with our RF Regulatory Licensing Manager, you will prepare and file earth station applications in the U.S. and internationally, support ITU filings, and keep a fast-growing licensing pipeline organized from customer request through grant and renewal. You will turn satellite and antenna technical data into regulator-ready filings, work with customers, outside counsel, and internal teams, and own the ticketing system that tracks every application. This is a hands-on role for an engineer who wants to work at the intersection of RF engineering, spectrum regulation, legal, and operations.

Responsibilities:

  • Prepare, file, and track earth station applications, modifications, amendments, special temporary authorities, and renewals before the FCC (Part 25 and Part 5 experimental) and international regulators such as ACMA (Australia) and BNetzA (Germany), working with outside counsel and filing agents.

  • Build the technical content of filings: link budgets, EIRP and EIRP density, G/T and system noise temperature, antenna gain patterns and off-axis compliance, emission designators, and RF hazard (EMF) analyses.

  • Support ITU filings for earth stations and customer satellite networks: assemble and check Appendix 4 data (SpaceCap/SpaceVal), track filing status, and keep national applications consistent with the underlying ITU filings.

  • Own the licensing Jira space day to day: triage new requests from Business Development, keep status, owners, due dates, and blockers current, and prepare the dashboard and metrics (drafted, filed, granted) for the weekly licensing meeting.

  • Serve as a technical point of contact for customers’ regulatory teams at intake: collect satellite, ITU filing, and authorization details, and flag gaps early (e.g., missing ITU filings, market access, or national authorizations).

  • Track post-grant obligations, including license conditions, frequency coordination with other operators, expirations, and renewals, and maintain the license register.

  • Support equipment certification and type approval of our S-, X-, and Ka-band antennas for import and licensing in multiple countries.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, aerospace engineering, physics, or a related field.

  • 3–6 years of experience in satellite communications, spectrum regulatory work, or RF systems engineering, including at least 2 years preparing regulatory filings.

  • Hands-on experience preparing U.S. earth station or space station applications (FCC Part 25 and/or Part 5) and applications in at least one non-U.S. jurisdiction.

  • Working knowledge of the ITU Radio Regulations as they apply to satellite networks and earth stations (including Articles 21 and 22 and Appendix 4), and experience preparing or reviewing ITU filing data.

  • Solid satellite link fundamentals: link budgets, EIRP, PSD, G/T, antenna patterns, and interference metrics such as C/I and I/N.

  • Experience managing many concurrent work items in Jira or a similar ticketing tool, with the discipline to keep status, owners, and dates current.

  • Clear technical writing for regulators, customers, and non-engineers.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Hands-on use of ITU BR software (SpaceCap, SpaceVal, TerRaSys) and experience with coordination requests or BR IFIC review.

  • Experience with FCC, NTIA, or other U.S. federal spectrum processes, or with government customers.

  • RF test and measurement experience (e.g., spectrum analyzer emissions measurements, antenna pattern testing), or equipment certification and type approval.

  • Background at a ground station, GSaaS, or NGSO operator; familiarity with S-, X-, and Ka-band TT&C and mission data links.

  • Jira configuration experience (workflows, filters, dashboards) and Confluence.

We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.



Role:

Northwood is hiring a Regulatory Engineer to help license our global ground station network. Working directly with our RF Regulatory Licensing Manager, you will prepare and file earth station applications in the U.S. and internationally, support ITU filings, and keep a fast-growing licensing pipeline organized from customer request through grant and renewal. You will turn satellite and antenna technical data into regulator-ready filings, work with customers, outside counsel, and internal teams, and own the ticketing system that tracks every application. This is a hands-on role for an engineer who wants to work at the intersection of RF engineering, spectrum regulation, legal, and operations.



Responsibilities:

 - Prepare, file, and track earth station applications, modifications, amendments, special temporary authorities, and renewals before the FCC (Part 25 and Part 5 experimental) and international regulators such as ACMA (Australia) and BNetzA (Germany), working with outside counsel and filing agents.

 - Build the technical content of filings: link budgets, EIRP and EIRP density, G/T and system noise temperature, antenna gain patterns and off-axis compliance, emission designators, and RF hazard (EMF) analyses.

 - Support ITU filings for earth stations and customer satellite networks: assemble and check Appendix 4 data (SpaceCap/SpaceVal), track filing status, and keep national applications consistent with the underlying ITU filings.

 - Own the licensing Jira space day to day: triage new requests from Business Development, keep status, owners, due dates, and blockers current, and prepare the dashboard and metrics (drafted, filed, granted) for the weekly licensing meeting.

 - Serve as a technical point of contact for customers’ regulatory teams at intake: collect satellite, ITU filing, and authorization details, and flag gaps early (e.g., missing ITU filings, market access, or national authorizations).

 - Track post-grant obligations, including license conditions, frequency coordination with other operators, expirations, and renewals, and maintain the license register.

 - Support equipment certification and type approval of our S-, X-, and Ka-band antennas for import and licensing in multiple countries.



Basic Qualifications:

 - Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, aerospace engineering, physics, or a related field.

 - 3–6 years of experience in satellite communications, spectrum regulatory work, or RF systems engineering, including at least 2 years preparing regulatory filings.

 - Hands-on experience preparing U.S. earth station or space station applications (FCC Part 25 and/or Part 5) and applications in at least one non-U.S. jurisdiction.

 - Working knowledge of the ITU Radio Regulations as they apply to satellite networks and earth stations (including Articles 21 and 22 and Appendix 4), and experience preparing or reviewing ITU filing data.

 - Solid satellite link fundamentals: link budgets, EIRP, PSD, G/T, antenna patterns, and interference metrics such as C/I and I/N.

 - Experience managing many concurrent work items in Jira or a similar ticketing tool, with the discipline to keep status, owners, and dates current.

 - Clear technical writing for regulators, customers, and non-engineers.



Preferred Qualifications:

 - Hands-on use of ITU BR software (SpaceCap, SpaceVal, TerRaSys) and experience with coordination requests or BR IFIC review.

 - Experience with FCC, NTIA, or other U.S. federal spectrum processes, or with government customers.

 - RF test and measurement experience (e.g., spectrum analyzer emissions measurements, antenna pattern testing), or equipment certification and type approval.

 - Background at a ground station, GSaaS, or NGSO operator; familiarity with S-, X-, and Ka-band TT&C and mission data links.

 - Jira configuration experience (workflows, filters, dashboards) and Confluence.

Role:

As Executive Assistant to the CEO at Northwood, you will serve as a highly trusted partner to our CEO, helping maximize their time, focus, and effectiveness as we build the internet for space. You will work closely with the CEO and partner with the broader executive office to ensure seamless coordination and support.

This is a dedicated, high-impact executive support role for someone who takes pride in mastering the craft of executive assistance. You will own the day-to-day operational complexity of supporting a CEO whose schedule spans company leadership, customers, investors, strategic partners, press, and other high-priority external engagements.

The pace is fast, the expectations are high, and priorities can change with little notice. Success requires exceptional judgment, attention to detail, responsiveness, discretion, and the ability to anticipate needs before they are articulated. You should be comfortable making thoughtful decisions independently, navigating ambiguity, and maintaining composure when multiple high-stakes priorities are moving simultaneously.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as a trusted gatekeeper, exercising sound judgment to manage competing requests, protect the CEO's time, and proactively resolve scheduling conflicts and shifting priorities.

  • Manage the CEO's inbox and communications, identifying urgent matters, drafting responses in their voice, and ensuring timely follow-through.

  • Act as a trusted liaison between the CEO and internal leadership, investors, customers, strategic partners, press, and other high-profile external stakeholders.

  • Own end-to-end domestic and international travel planning, including complex itineraries, logistics, and last-minute changes, providing responsive support as needs arise.

  • Anticipate the CEO's needs and ensure they are prepared for key engagements by coordinating meeting materials, briefings, relevant context, and logistical details.

  • Track executive commitments, action items, and outstanding requests, proactively driving resolution and escalating critical matters when appropriate.

  • Develop a deep understanding of the CEO's priorities, working style, and key relationships to operate with increasing independence, exercising exceptional judgment, discretion, and professionalism in all interactions.

Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of progressive Executive Assistant experience, including direct support for a CEO, founder, or C-level executive in a demanding, fast-paced environment.

  • Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and sound judgment, with a proven ability to independently manage complex priorities, anticipate needs, and solve problems with limited direction.

jobs.title: Development Test Engineer (Prism)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role:

Northwood is looking for an engineer to build the development systems that ensure our hardware performs reliably from early prototypes through operations. You’ll own development test including hardware-in-the-loop testbeds, development RF testbeds or ranges/chambers, and customer integration milestones for modem test. This is a highly hands-on role that sits at the intersection of electronics, software, and systems integration — ideal for someone who enjoys turning ambiguous problems into robust, repeatable test capabilities that help develop world-class systems.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Lead integrated test development from concept through operations, including test strategy, requirements, and execution plans

  • Run qualification and hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) campaigns

  • Own the path to certification for EMI/EMC and other applicable standards (e.g., MIL-STD-461, FCC/CE), including pre-compliance testing, design-for-compliance input to the hardware team, test lab coordination, and certification documentation

  • Design hardware, wiring, and electrical systems to support electrical and RF testing for development and production (fixtures, harnesses, interfaces, rack integration)

  • Create device and subsystem simulators for hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) and integrate testbeds into our CI/CD pipeline

  • Design production test setups and execute low quantity production tests for rapid manufacturing cycles

  • Own test maintainability and reliability across the lifecycle, defining calibration, upkeep, debugging, and continuous improvement of test assets

 

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, or related field

  • Hands-on experience in Linux-based environment, and familiarity with basic computer networking

  • Hands-on experience with electrical test equipment such as power supplies, DC loads, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and spectrum analyzers

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience root-causing issues in integrated electronics (mixed-signal, digital, RF-adjacent systems)

  • Hands-on EMC test and troubleshooting experience, such as near-field probes, radiated emissions testing

  • Familiarity with MIL-STD-461 EMI/EMC requirements and MIL-STD-810 environmental test methods, including vibration, shock, and thermal testing

  • Experience building RF test setups for communications systems, including over-the-air and conducted testing, channel emulation, and modem or link-level performance characterization

  • Experience building hardware-in-the-loop testbeds and device simulators, and running them in automated CI environments

  • Experience designing test racks and harnessing

 

Compensation:

Test Engineer/Level 2: $100,000-$119,000 per year

Test Engineer/Level 3: $118,000-$148,000 per year

Test Engineer/Level 4: $136,000-$170,000 per year

Additional Information:

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

jobs.title: SMT Technician
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role:

We are seeking a Surface-Mount Technology (SMT) Technician to own the setup, programming, and performance of our surface mount line across production and new product introduction (NPI) builds. This role is critical to delivering high-reliability electronics on schedule and at scale, with direct impact on our ability to deploy next-generation space communication systems. You will keep print, placement, reflow, and inspection equipment running at peak performance, catch defects before they move downstream, and work closely with Engineering to turn new designs into repeatable, high-yield builds.

Responsibilities

  • Set up and operate SMT equipment, including screen printers, pick-and-place, reflow ovens, SPI, AOI, and X-ray, including feeder setup, component verification, and changeovers per work instructions

  • Create, debug, and optimize programs for pick-and-place, screen printer, SPI, AOI, and X-ray equipment

  • Configure and tune process parameters such as nozzles, conveyor speeds, print settings, and reflow profiles

  • Perform preventive maintenance, cleaning, calibration, and repairs, and partner with Engineering to diagnose and resolve equipment issues

  • Inspect solder quality using microscopes, AOI, and X-ray to IPC-A-610 standards, documenting defects and root causes

  • Support production and NPI builds, assist technicians and Engineering with technical issues, and drive continuous improvement of SOPs and processes


Basic Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent

  • 5+ years of experience in SMT electronics manufacturing

  • Hands-on experience operating and setting up SMT equipment (screen printer, pick-and-place, reflow, and inspection)

  • Experience programming or editing programs on SMT placement or inspection equipment

  • Experience building to travelers, BOMs, work instructions, and assembly drawings


Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiar with IPC-A-610 and/or J-STD-001

  • Experience with Fuji placement, Heller reflow, and Nordson CyberOptics SPI/AOI equipment

  • Experience in high-reliability, aerospace, or IPC Class 3 electronics manufacturing

  • Experience with fine-pitch and BGA components, including X-ray inspection of hidden solder joints


Additional Requirements

  • This role requires being on-site 5 days per week

  • Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed

  • Must be able to lift and carry up to 25 lbs. unassisted

  • Repetitive assembly operations, grasping, standing, lifting, bending, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position

jobs.title: Infrastructure Engineer (Platform)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role
Northwood runs a global network of phased array ground stations supported by cloud infrastructure; clusters that run mission software, identity systems every service depends on, the observability stack that tells operators what is happening at every site, and the IaC that defines all of it. The Infrastructure Engineer – Cloud owns and operates that environment.
This is a core individual contributor role on the Infrastructure team. You take a defined scope, run it independently, and bring real depth in cloud infrastructure. You'll work directly with Platform software engineers building the services and config models that describe what the environment should be. You'll make that intent real in cloud infrastructure, and keep it running.

Responsibilities

  • Own and operate all components of the cloud infrastructure stack: cloud accounts, hosted k8s clusters, CA, secrets, IAM, the observability pipeline. Take a defined scope and execute it without ongoing oversight.

  • Build and maintain infrastructure as code. Define and implement GitOps practices and proper CI gates to test, audit, and approve infrastructure changes.

  • Implement cloud-side networking: VPCs, transit route tables, VPNs and Direct Connect attachments, egress and ingress inspection. Partner with the network engineering on cloud to site handoff.

  • Carry on-call for the cloud stack. Resolve the majority of incidents independently and run post-incident reviews for the ones you own.
